([[Apopka, Florida]]) | college = [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] (2017–2020) | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] ([[2019–20 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2020]]) * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]] ([[2018–19 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2019]]) }} '''Paul Reed''' (born June 14, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul Blue Demons]]. ==Early life and high school career== Reed grew up in [[Orlando, Florida]] and attended [[Wekiva High School]]. Reed grew from being 6'2 as freshman in high school to 6'6 as a junior and was 6'8 by the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-hs-paul-reed-basketball-0730-20160729-story.html|title=Basketball report: Wekiva's Paul Reed on radar for UCF, others|first=Buddy|last=Collings|work=Orlando Sentinel|date=July 29, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 18.2 points and 11.4 rebounds and was named the Central Florida Player of the Year as he led the Mustangs to the state championship game.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/DePaul-Officially-Inks-Paul-Reed-for-2017-74913289/|title=DePaul Officially Inks Paul Reed for 2017|website=247Sports.com|access-date=December 10, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-boys-basketball-all-area-0319-story.html|title=Paul Reed leads All-Central Florida boys basketball teams|work=Orlando Sentinel|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2019}} Rated a three-star recruit and the No. 235 prospect in his class, Reed committed to play college basketball at DePaul over offers from [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] and [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]].{{cite web|url=http://thecatchandshoot.com/depaul-adds-paul-reed-to-2017-class/|title=DePaul adds 3-star Paul Reed to 2017 class|first=Jesse|last=Kramer|website=TheCatchAndShoot.com|date=December 4, 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/12/5/20996865/depaul-basketball-ncaa-tournament-rankings-texas-tech-2020|title=DePaul basketball’s dream resurgence is finally real|first=Ricky|last=O'Donnell|website=[[SB Nation]]|date=December 5, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}} ==College career== As a true freshman, Reed averaged 3.6 points and 3.1 rebounds in 28 games played off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://depauliaonline.com/39318/sports/hard-work-pays-off-in-year-two-for-paul-reed/|title=Hard work pays off in year two for Paul Reed|first=Evan|last=Sully|work=The DePaulia|date=February 18, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}} He received more playing time towards the end of the season and averaged 5.6 points and 4.6 rebounds over the final 14 games of the season.{{cite web|url=https://depauliaonline.com/31836/sports/unheralded-freshman-shows-late-season-promise/|title=Unheralded freshman shows late season promise|first=Paul|last=Steeno|work=The DePaulia|date=February 26, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2019}} As a sophomore, Reed averaged 12.3 points and a [[Big East Conference]]-leading 8.5 rebounds per game and was named the Big East Conference [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Most Improved Player]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/Paul-Reed-is-Most-Improved-in-the-Big-East-129961743/|title=Paul Reed is Most Improved in the Big East|first=Steve|last=Newhouse|website=247Sports.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/1439624/2019/12/06/searching-for-siakam-heres-a-big-wing-with-sleeper-potential-that-the-warriors-could-consider-in-the-2020-nba-draft/|title=Searching for Siakam: Here’s a big wing with sleeper potential that the Warriors could consider in the 2020 NBA Draft|first=Ethan|last=Strauss|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=December 6, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}} In the [[2019 College Basketball Invitational]] Reed averaged 18.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, 2.7 blocks, and 2.2 steals as he helped lead the Blue Demons to the best-of-three final.{{cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/10/15/big-east-basketball-20-interesting-people-2019-20-season/3/|title=Big East Basketball: 20 most interesting people of 2019-20 season|first=Brian|last=Foley|website=BustingBrackets.com|publisher=FanSided|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}} Reed entered his junior season as a preseason All-Big East selection.{{cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/2019/12/09/depaul-paul-reed-scouting-report-nba-draft-analysis/|title=DePaul big man Paul Reed is one of NCAA's most underrated prospects|first=Bryan|last=Kalbrosky|website=Hoops Hype|publisher=USA Today|date=December 9, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019}} Reed recorded ten double-doubles and was named to the Big East Weekly Honor Roll four times during DePaul's 13-game non-conference schedule at the start of the season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/DePauls-Paul-Reed-Blossoming-in-Junior-Season-140241445/|title=DePaul’s Paul Reed Blossoming in Junior Season|first=Scott|last=Phillips|website=247Sports.com|date=December 10, 2019|access-date=December 23, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://depaulbluedemons.com/news/2019/12/16/mens-basketball-big-east-honors-paul-reed-once-again.aspx|title=BIG EAST Honors Paul Reed Once Again|website=DePaulBlueDemons.com|date=December 16, 2019|access-date=December 23, 2019}} Reed scored 23 points on 8-of-9 shooting with nine rebounds in DePaul's 79–66 upset of No. 5 [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] on January 18.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/01/18/depaul-upsets-top-five-butler-paul-reed|title=Paul Reed's 23 Points Lead DePaul to Upset Over No. 5 Butler|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=February 3, 2020}} Reed missed several games in February and March with a hip pointer injury.{{cite news |last1=Newhouse |first1=Steve |title=Providence Routs DePaul |url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/Providence-Friars-Rout-DePaul-Blue-Demons-on-Senior-Day-144738988/ |accessdate=March 8, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 7, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Reed was named Second Team All-Big East after averaging 15.1 points and finishing second in the conference in rebounds (10.7), blocks (2.6) and steals (1.9).{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=Xavier basketball players honored on All-Big East Conference teams |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/03/08/xavier-basketball-gets-4-players-all-conference-team/4994440002/ |accessdate=March 8, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=March 8, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/DePauls-Paul-Reed-Named-All-Big-East-Second-Team-144779680/|title=DePaul’s Paul Reed Named All-Big East Second Team|first=Steve|last=Newhouse|website=247Sports.com|date=March 8, 2020|access-date=March 16, 2020}} He had 18 double-doubles for the season. After the season, Reed declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], forgoing his final season of eligibility.{{cite news |title=DePaul junior Paul Reed declares for NBA Draft |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/3/28/21198392/depaul-junior-paul-reed-declares-for-nba-draft |accessdate=March 29, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=March 28, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] | 28 || 1 || 9.9 || .518 || .214 || .579 || 3.1 || .4 || .5 || .5 || 3.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] | '''36''' || 28 || 26.9 || '''.562''' || '''.405''' || '''.770''' || 8.5 || .9 || 1.1 || 1.5 || 12.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] | 29 || '''29''' || '''31.7''' || .516 || .308 || .738 || '''10.7''' || '''1.6''' || '''1.9''' || '''2.6''' || '''15.1''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 93 || 58 || 23.2 || .535 || .330 || .739 || 7.5 || 1.0 || 1.2 || 1.5 || 10.6 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://depaulbluedemons.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/paul-reed/1869 DePaul Blue Demons bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Reed, Paul}} [[Category:1999 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Florida]] [[Category:DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball players]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Orlando, Florida]]
